1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator entropy source configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a permutation circuit configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function to generate a second entropy value;
a pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value and configured to generate a random number; and
an encryption circuit configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number, wherein the encryption circuit is physically distinct from the ring oscillator entropy source and the permutation circuit.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the encryption circuit is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the encryption circuit is configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises at least one ring oscillator.

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation circuit applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the permutation circuit is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation circuit comprises a hash function circuit configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation circuit comprises a bit-mixer circuit configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the permutation circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator entropy source;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number with an encryption circuit physically distinct from the ring oscillator entropy source.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises at least one ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the at least one ring oscillator.

17. (Cancelled)

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator entropy source comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent ring oscillators.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Previously presented) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
